Congenital Zika Syndrome and Other Birth Defects For Everyone Oct. 26, 2026 What to know Zika virus can spread from an infected pregnant woman to her fetus. Infection during pregnancy can lead to congenital Zika syndrome and other birth defects. Zika virus infection does not impact future pregnancies. Overview of Zika-associated birth defects Zika virus infection during pregnancy can cause birth defects of the brain or eye. These birth defects can occur alone or with developmental problems in a particular pattern called congenital Zika syndrome. The following conditions can occur in a baby with congenital Zika virus infection: Smaller than expected head size, called microcephaly Problems with brain development Feeding problems, such as difficulty swallowing Hearing loss and vision problems Seizures Decreased joint movement, called contractures Stiff muscles, making it difficult to move Not all babies born with congenital Zika syndrome will have all of these conditions. Discover how today's digital infrastructure is shaping the cities of yesterday and tomorrow. 12:23 The complexity of some cities’ architecture makes modernization a different kind of challenge entirely. Video by Nicely Done Productions By Sam Kent Last updated August 12, 2026 Cities are constantly evolving. They are built up, layer by layer, each generation leaving its mark on the one before. Roman roads became the foundation for medieval streets. Aqueducts gave way to railways, electricity, and underground transportation. Over time, every city’s infrastructure becomes a record of the people who shaped it years before. Walk through Rome, and the history is impossible to ignore. Ancient walls sit beside modern apartments; the remains of a long-gone empire lie under busy streets. Layers of the past can be felt everywhere: yet Rome, just like every great city, cannot stand still. Today, millions of visitors and residents move through the city, expecting to stay connected above and below ground. From GPS and wayfinding tools to digital tickets and tap-to-pay features for transport systems, to instant communication between families and friends. The challenge is that today’s expectations for connectivity must be woven into yesterday’s infrastructure, without damaging what lies beneath. It's easier to control rodents before they can establish themselves in your home or building. Regularly check your home for rodent droppings and gnaw marks as these are both signs of a rodent's presence. Overview Rodents, such as rats, mice, and chipmunks, are known to carry many diseases. These diseases can spread to people directly, through: Handling of rodents Contact with rodent droppings (poop), urine, or saliva Rodent bites Rodent droppings, urine, and saliva can spread by breathing in air or eating food that is contaminated with rodent waste. Rodents can also carry ticks, mites, or fleas that can spread diseases. Many diseases do not cause any apparent illness in rodents. Three months after his wedding, Faisal Shahzad's home in rural Punjab is bursting with gifts from his bride's family, as part of the dowry. But the most prized possession is tucked under the bed: a 340W solar panel. "In the summer we ran it from 08:00 in the morning until the evening," he says, adding they didn't need to use grid power at all during the day. "We ran our air cooler on it all day." Pakistan has seen a boom in imported solar panels, which glisten from the rooftops of homes and hospitals; from farmers' fields to industrial complexes. From 2018 to 2025, the share of electricity generated from solar energy in the country rose from 1% to 28%, according to Pakistan-based think tank Renewables First, with some seven million households now owning panels. People used to gift motorbikes or other household items at weddings, Shahzad says. "Now they give a solar panel and an air cooler. It has almost become a must." pages.description: The US government is trying to find out whether the chaos was caused by "incompetence" or faulty equipment.
pages.text: Copper wire upgrade behind US flight suspension, transport secretary says Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Weather Newsletters Copper wire upgrade behind US flight suspension, transport secretary says 3 days ago Share Save Add as preferred on Google George Wright and Helen Davidson Watch: US ground stop caused by issue during copper wire update, transport secretary says A nationwide US ground stop that caused thousands of flight cancellations and prompted travel chaos was caused by a technical issue following a copper wire upgrade, the transport secretary has said. Sean Duffy told a news conference that the government was trying to find out whether the problem that led to air traffic controllers suspending take-offs for four hours on Friday had been caused by "incompetence" on the part of the company doing the upgrades or faulty equipment. Though the ground stop was lifted on Friday evening, it had a knock-on effect on air travel on Saturday as airlines attempted to clear a backlog of flights. Officials including Duffy had previously attributed the issue to outdated equipment. Maintenance on US air traffic control systems was being carried out to switch from copper wire to fibre-optic cable by a contractor called L3Harris, a technology provider, Duffy said. The US had "an incredibly old telecommunications system", he said, adding: "It was such an old wire that it was being discontinued." Gardaí (Irish police) said the man sustained critical wounds during the assault at Lower Glanmire Road at about 13:30 local time on Tuesday, which Irish broadcaster RTÉ has reported was a stabbing. He was transferred to Cork University Hospital for urgent medical attention, where he later died. Two males, an adult teenager and a juvenile, have been arrested in connection with the investigation, gardai said. A post-mortem will be carried out on Wednesday at Cork University Hospital. The investigation is being coordinated from an incident room at Mayfield Garda Station under the direction of a Senior Investigating Officer. Gardaí are appealing for witnesses to come forward. Knowable Magazine Schizophrenia is tough to diagnose. Patients may present with hallucinations (sometimes), social withdrawal (maybe) or delusions (not always). More generally, they just sound unlike themselves. Clinicians rely on their expertise and subtle cues to determine how different patients’ speech is, along with which symptoms appear over time, to justify leaning toward schizophrenia rather than another mental illness. This leads to delays in diagnosis. Americans with psychotic disorders—more than three million of whom have schizophrenia— receive a diagnosis a year and a half, on average, after their first symptoms appear. Despite what's depicted in movies and books, the real Tyrannosaurus rex was likely an awkward swimmer at best. Illustration by Fotokita, Getty Images By Riley Black Published July 2, 2025 When Michael Crichton released the novel Jurassic Park in 1990, he included a terrifying chase through one of the park’s ponds. Fictional paleontologist Alan Grant, looking after kids Lex and Tim, tries to sneak by a dozing Tyrannosaurus rex and motor across a lake away from the dinosaur. The T. rex follows, swimming after them like “the biggest crocodile in the world.” The scene stood out so much that it’s been revamped for the new movie Jurassic World: Rebirth . But while tyrannosaurs might swim in movies and books, could they swim in real life? Carnivorous dinosaurs are not generally thought of as good swimmers. During much of the 20 th century, in fact, paleontologists wrongly assumed that herbivorous dinosaurs ran into rivers and lakes to avoid the jaws of T. rex , Allosaurus , and other predators. No one had found any direct evidence that such carnivores could swim. But the discovery of dinosaur swim tracks at fossil sites around the world have indicated that theropod dinosaurs—the group that contains T. rex , birds, and their relatives—were more aquatically adept than suspected and may have even done their own version of the doggy paddle. The Great Bubble Barrier Amsterdam’s Westerdok looks like many other outlets to the city’s historic canals. But look past the familiar boats and birds, and there is a distinct pattern in the water not found elsewhere in the city: a diagonal line of whiter water. That’s because an innovative “curtain,” known technically as a Bubble Barrier, lies below the surface. On the bottom of the waterway is a perforated tube which pumps air out, directing plastic to the surface. The natural flow of water then carries plastic litter to the Bubble Barrier’s catchment system, an aluminum trap on one side of the waterway, to prevent it from making its way to the North Sea. “Anything you can think of that people have in the city, we’ve seen here,” Philip Ehrhorn, co-founder and chief technological officer of the Great Bubble Barrier , the company behind the technology, told me as we surveyed the barrier on a warm day in September. pages.text: Cricket Australia sets up 'safe space' for players to share sandpapergate experiences - BBC Sport Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Cricket Australia hopes the 'forum' will help the sport move on By Simon Atkinson and Tiffanie Turnbull Sydney Published 18 November 2026, 03:52 GMT Updated 1 hour ago Cricket Australia has launched an independent "forum" for players and staff involved in the sandpapergate scandal to share their version of events. In a memoir released earlier this month, former player Usman Khawaja claimed the entire Australia team knew of the plot to tamper with the ball during a 2018 Test in South Africa, contradicting the investigation at the time. His comments have led to a bitter split among former and current players and have overshadowed the beginning of Australia's international cricket season. The forum was not a new investigation and there will be no new penalties, Cricket Australia said, adding that nobody would be forced to take part. However, chief executive Todd Greenberg said he hoped the discussions would allow the sport to "move on". "The game is genuinely hurting at the moment. It's not good for anyone," he said. "We need to find a path through and we need some time to heal." The sandpapergate scandal is often described as one of Australian cricket's darkest days and was a source of national shame.
